Region-level ANOVA: compare protein states within residue regions

Source: R/compare_regions.R
compare_regions.Rd

Tests whether protein states differ in deuterium uptake within each region you define. Each peptide acts as its own control: the state effect is a two-way ANOVA uptake ~ peptide + state on the per-peptide mean uptake (replicates averaged), so it is the uptake difference within peptides, averaged over the region's peptides, judged against how consistent that difference is from peptide to peptide (peptides are the replication unit, as in a randomized-block / repeated-measures design; with two states this is a paired t-test of the per-peptide differences). This is far more powerful than pooling peptide means into one distribution per state (as compare_states_unmatched() must do when peptide maps differ), because differences between peptides (length, location) are removed before the states are compared.

Usage

compare_regions(
  filepath,
  times,
  regions,
  states = NULL,
  reference = NULL,
  by = c("sequence", "position"),
  replicates = NULL,
  percent = FALSE,
  time_model = FALSE,
  p_adjust = "none"
)

Arguments

filepath

input file or table, as for output_tp().

times

one or more Deut.Time values. Default: all.

regions

named list of c(start, end) residue ranges, e.g. list(NTR = c(1, 85), ACD = c(86, 165)). A peptide belongs to a region when it lies entirely inside it.

states

states to compare (two or more). Default: all.

reference

optional state; pairwise contrasts are then only reference vs each other state.

by

peptide matching between states: "sequence" (default) or "position", as in compare_states_tp().

replicates

optional maximum number of replicates per state.

percent

value scale, as in output_tp(): FALSE (Da, default), TRUE, "FD" or "per_residue".

time_model

FALSE (default): one model per region and time point. TRUE: one model per region over all times (needs two or more).

p_adjust

multiple-testing correction passed to stats::p.adjust(): "none" (default) or e.g. "BH".

Value

a list of two data frames. summary: one row per region (and time point): region, Deut.Time ("all" with time_model = TRUE), n_peptides, n_obs, F_state, df_state, df_resid, p_state, p_state_adj, p_state_x_peptide, and with time_model = TRUE also p_state_x_time. pairs: one row per region, time and state pair: estimate (Da, or percent, state2 - state1), se, p_value, p_adj.

Details

Requires the same peptides in every compared state (matched peptides, as for output_tp()); peptides missing from any state are left out of that region. For states with different peptide maps use compare_states_unmatched().

For each region (and time point) the result reports:

  • an F-test of the state effect (do the states differ at all in this region; with two states it is the test of their difference),

  • an F-test of the state x peptide interaction on the replicate values (does the state effect differ between peptides of the region by more than replicate noise - a significant value means the effect is localized or mixed in direction, so the average shift alone does not describe the region; look at the peptides with compare_states_tp() or plot_fissure_vent()),

  • pairwise state contrasts: average shift (Da, state2 - state1) per peptide with its standard error and t-test p-value from the model.

With several time points and time_model = TRUE, one model per region is fitted over all of them on the per-peptide-and-time means, uptake ~ peptide * time + state, testing the state effect averaged over time, plus whether it changes with time (state x time).

A region needs at least two peptides. Every peptide weighs equally, whatever its replicate noise. p-values are raw by default; p_adjust corrects across all regions (and time points), and separately across all pairwise contrasts.

See also

compare_states_tp() (peptide by peptide), compare_states_unmatched() (different peptide maps), residue_regions() (regions found from the data)

Examples

file_nm <- system.file("extdata", "All_results_table.csv", package = "HDXBoxeR")
res <- compare_regions(file_nm, times = "1800.00s",
                       regions = list(nterm = c(1, 100), cterm = c(101, 225)))
res$summary
#>   region Deut.Time n_peptides n_obs   F_state df_state df_resid    p_state
#> 1  nterm  1800.00s          9    54  4.012432        1        8 0.08012977
#> 2  cterm  1800.00s         20   120 17.078329        1       19 0.00056602
#>   p_state_adj p_state_x_peptide
#> 1  0.08012977      7.621526e-28
#> 2  0.00056602      2.886840e-24
res$pairs
#>   region Deut.Time  state1 state2   estimate         se    p_value      p_adj
#> 1  nterm  1800.00s Unbound  bound -0.3596296 0.17953604 0.08012977 0.08012977
#> 2  cterm  1800.00s Unbound  bound -0.2543000 0.06153521 0.00056602 0.00056602
